application_artifact.bundle_type_stamp_note: The post-bundle release executable is rewritten by Tauri after bundling and carries no signature (4,303,872 bytes against 4,319,520 for the signed, installer-embedded one). sha256 is the installer-embedded identity; check signatures in the installer or the installed files.

source.note: the version bump is committed before the build, so this commit and tree are the ones the binary was made from

superseded.supersedes: 0.1.0-beta.10 (published 2026-09-30, unsigned; installer e763023e…, embedded e0db6efc…). The β.10 release is not changed.

contents_since_beta10: Authenticode signatures (SHA-256, RFC 3161 timestamp from http://timestamp.acs.microsoft.com) on the installer, the application, the uninstaller and the NSIS plugins Tauri bundles; signer CN=wi-t.com Inc., O=wi-t.com Inc., L=Yokohama, S=Kanagawa-ken, C=JP (Azure Artifact Signing, account witcomsigning, profile witcomPublicTrust)

the build says how it is signed from one value, SAKU_CODE_SIGNING: the Home footer reads 「CODE_SIGNING = AZURE_ARTIFACT_SIGNING」, and resources/build-metadata.json and the host's get_runtime_state.code_signing say the same
version 0.1.0-beta.10.1; the manual's last-checked day is 2026-10-02 (Windows 10.0.26300, WebView2 Runtime 154.0.4258.48)

provisional_wording.note: docs/collaboration/provisional-wording.json has no entries: every user-visible string in this build has been through ライター&SNS 様式チェック, and the English is the 英語翻訳チーム delivery.

release_state.note: Signed (Authenticode, Azure Artifact Signing, wi-t.com Inc.) / NOT_RELEASED until the Owner publishes. A signature shows who made the file and that it has not changed since signing; it does not show that the contents are correct or safe.

code_signing.signer: CN=wi-t.com Inc., O=wi-t.com Inc., L=Yokohama, S=Kanagawa-ken, C=JP
code_signing.timestamp: http://timestamp.acs.microsoft.com (TSA: Microsoft Public RSA Time Stamping Authority)
code_signing.tool: signtool from Windows SDK 10.0.26100.0 (x64) with Azure.CodeSigning.Dlib (Microsoft.Azure.ArtifactSigningClientTools 0.1.128), via Tauri bundle.windows.signCommand
not_signed: LangDLL.dll — an NSIS plugin Tauri does not sign; it is extracted at install time only

signing_override.note: The signing override actually used is written outside the repository at build time, because it holds host paths (signtool, the Artifact Signing dlib and its metadata.json); this template is that file with the paths replaced by placeholders.
